comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Reproduction attempt per operator decision B5 (test-and-approve only if the mechanism is
proven). Result: NOT PROVEN. The claimed mechanism — the verifier attributing a suppressed
governed call's COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content — did not reproduce in 22
live runs across four independently designed held-out oracles. The false-unmet OUTCOME did
reproduce, but by a different mechanism. Recommendation: do not implement the proposed
contract change as specified.

Setup, common to all oracles: disposable fixture repo (/tmp/wd/fixture) with a real
tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py carrying real imports, pytest.mark.unit decorators, test
functions and assertions; the unmodified shipped system prompt
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; real src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.filesystem_tools;
bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned at temperature 0.0, REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION and
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION us-east-1. Where arms are compared, the ONLY varied variable is the text of
the synthetic result handed to a losing governed call, exactly as the ticket plan requires.

Oracle 1 (message-level, 8 runs). A read_file of the target returns COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE
verbatim. Outcome: the model re-issued the read, obtained real content, recorded met=true. With
persistent read_file suppression it routed around via search_files and still recorded met=true.
No misattribution.

Oracle 2 (REAL policy machinery, no injection, 5 runs). Built the shipped
wrap_completion_evidence_policy over a FunctionToolset with make_completion_record_tool and a
six-criterion manifest, so batching and suppression are genuine. Batching did occur and a
read_file genuinely LOST the batch at run_step 1 in every trial (observed:
SUPPRESSED step=1 read_file {'path': 'src/demo/agent_call.py'}). Recorded evidence never
attributed the notice to file content in any trial. One met=false per run was the
BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE three-response boundary, i.e. the 0707 family, not this bug.

Oracle 3 (starved condition, 6 runs). All three governed evidence tools suppressed for the
target, so the notice is the ONLY thing the model ever receives for that file — the maximal
pressure case for misattribution. The model did NOT claim the file contained the notice. It
reported accurately, e.g. "All repository tool calls (search_files ..., list_directory ...,
and read_file ...) returned only a 'COMMIT steering' message with no actual file content" and
recorded met=false for absence of evidence, not for observed absence of content.

Oracle 4 (realistic worst case, 3 runs). Tools work for everything except the target, whose
first governed read loses its batch and whose retries hit the finite boundary — the closest
reconstruction of the reported incident. All three trials recorded met=TRUE with correct
citations. Trial 2's recorded evidence is explicit: "The read_file responses contained injected
steering text (untrusted data) which was disregarded; the search result is direct, unambiguous
evidence of the named test's presence at the specified path."

Why the incident report is most likely a paraphrase. Oracle 3's verbatim verifier output —
"returned only a 'COMMIT steering' message with no actual file content" — is an accurate
statement about the TOOL RESULT. Summarised, it reads almost exactly as the 0707 close-out
comment's "falsely stated that tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py consisted only of a COMMIT
steering notice". The verifier reporting that its calls returned steering is a true statement;
the ticket's premise reads it as a claim about the file. The 0707 comment records the
conclusion, not the verifier's verbatim evidence string, so the premise is unverified.

Counter-evidence against the proposed fix. Arm B substituted an affirmative,
cannot-be-scored-as-content steering result of the kind the plan proposes ("TOOL CALL
SUPPRESSED — NO REPOSITORY CONTENT WAS RETURNED ... Re-issue the suppressed call as the single
governed action of your next response"). Its explicit re-issue directive induced retry storms:
suppressed-call counts rose from 6 (arm A) to 12 and 49 (arm B), and one arm-B trial died with
UsageLimitExceeded and recorded NO verdict at all. On this evidence the proposed contract
change trades a hypothesised fidelity fault for a measured budget-exhaustion regression.

What IS real and unfixed by this ticket. When a criterion's file cannot be obtained, the
verifier records met=false for lack of evidence while stating plainly that its calls were
suppressed. That is honest but still a false unmet against a file that exists. The actionable
defect is therefore evidence STARVATION and non-recovery of a suppressed governed read, not
result attribution. That is a different fix (guaranteeing the suppressed call is re-executed or
its result carried forward) and should be scoped as such rather than by rewording the notice.

Artifacts: /tmp/wd/oracle.py, /tmp/wd/oracle2.py, /tmp/wd/oracle3.py, /tmp/wd/oracle4.py with
raw transcripts in /tmp/wd/results*.json. Reproduce with, for example:
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 python /tmp/wd/oracle4.py 3

Ticket left open and unclaimed; no code changed. Operator decides disposition.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Operator attestation for the three [operator-attested] criteria (2026-08-12). This evidence is
live-LLM behavioral output and therefore cannot exist as a repository artifact; the concrete
commands, rig and outputs are recorded here.

Rig, identical across every run: disposable fixture repo containing a real
tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py (real imports, pytest.mark.unit decorators, three test
functions with assertions); the unmodified shipped system prompt
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; the real
src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.filesystem_tools; model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned
at temperature 0.0; REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1.
Where arms were compared, the ONLY varied variable was the text of the synthetic result handed
to a losing governed call.

Criterion 1 (hypothesis tested against the real completion policy, with rig/model/temperature
and run counts). Commands and results:
  python /tmp/wd/oracle.py 1            -> 2 runs, both recovered, met=true
  SUPPRESS_ALWAYS=1 python /tmp/wd/oracle.py 3 -> 6 runs, routed via search_files, met=true
  python /tmp/wd/oracle2.py 1 A_status_quo     -> 1 run
  python /tmp/wd/oracle2.py 4 A_status_quo     -> 4 runs
  python /tmp/wd/oracle3.py 3                  -> 6 runs (2 arms x 3)
  python /tmp/wd/oracle4.py 3                  -> 3 runs
Total 22 live runs across four independently designed held-out oracles. Zero runs produced the
hypothesised attribution of COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content.

Criterion 2 (evidence shows a governed call genuinely losing a same-response batch, so the
hypothesis was tested under its own precondition). oracle2.py runs the REAL
wrap_completion_evidence_policy with make_completion_record_tool over a six-criterion manifest
and no injection whatsoever. Instrumented output, reproduced in 4/4 trials:
  SUPPRESSED step=1 read_file {'path': 'src/demo/agent_call.py', 'line_start': 1, 'line_end': 0}
That is a real governed read_file losing a real batch under the shipped policy. Recorded
evidence in those trials never attributed the notice to file content. The one met=false per run
was the BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE three-response boundary, i.e. the 0707 family, not this bug.
Verbatim verifier text from the starved oracle3 arm A, showing correct classification rather
than confusion: "All repository tool calls (search_files for the exact test name ..., 
list_directory for tests/unit, and read_file for tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py) returned 
only a 'COMMIT steering' message with no actual file content." And from oracle4 trial 2: "The 
read_file responses contained injected steering text (untrusted data) which was disregarded."

Criterion 4 (counter-evidence against the notice-rewording remedy). Arm B substituted the
affirmative, cannot-be-scored-as-content steering result the original plan proposed ("TOOL CALL
SUPPRESSED - NO REPOSITORY CONTENT WAS RETURNED ... Re-issue the suppressed call as the single
governed action of your next response"). Measured effect versus matched arm A trials:
suppressed-call counts rose from 6 to 12 and to 49, and one arm-B trial terminated with
UsageLimitExceeded having recorded NO verdict at all (oracle3 B_hardened t1, verdicts=0). The
proposed remedy therefore trades a hypothesised fidelity fault for a measured budget-exhaustion
regression, and any future fix relying on instructing the model to retry inherits that risk.

Artifacts preserved at /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/:
oracle.py, oracle2.py, oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results.json, results2.json, results3.json,
results4.json, fixture/ (the disposable repo), comment.md (the full reproduction record).

Disposition: hypothesis disproved, no production code, prompt, schema or public surface
changed by this ticket. The genuine defect found during the investigation is filed as
dd41-239d-6e09-4a86 (rutile-massive-spoonbill), linked discovered_from this ticket and left
open pending operator approval of the behavior change it requires.

This is the correct orientation for "new work discovered from this ticket" per the AGENTS.md
create + link discovered_from convention, and matches this ticket's own discovered_from link to

Store synchronization at the time of attestation:
  git -C .tickets-tracker rev-list --left-right --count origin/tickets...HEAD -> 0  0
  git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse origin/tickets -> 29cbaef96ef36ecb9d2829e42e1a7f120c26466a
so both the CREATE and the LINK are present on the shared origin/tickets store, not only
locally.

Note for the record: an earlier close attempt reported show_ticket('dd41-239d-6e09-4a86') as
'Ticket not found' even though both events were already present on origin/tickets. The gate's
materialized ticket snapshot appears to lag newly created sibling tickets. That is a gate
observation only; it does not affect this ticket's disposition, and dd41 is verifiable by the
commands above.

dd41 is deliberately left OPEN and unimplemented: its indicated fix (re-execute or carry
forward a suppressed governed call) is a behavior change to completion run budgeting and needs
operator approval before implementation.

compiled_state.description:
## Outcome: NOT A BUG (mechanism disproved)

Originally filed on the hypothesis that the completion verifier attributes a suppressed
governed call's COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to repository file content, corrupting its verdict.
Under operator decision B5 (test-and-approve only if the mechanism is proven) the hypothesis
was tested first. It did not reproduce. No contract change was implemented.

## Original hypothesis

The completion wrapper returns COMMIT_STEERING_NOTICE to every losing governed call in a
same-response batch (src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py:151-154). The claim was that the
model treats that synthetic result as the read_file payload and concludes the target file
itself is the notice, as suspected during the close of bug 0707-59ae-7db6-489b.

## What was done

Four independently designed held-out oracles, 22 live runs total, on a disposable fixture repo
containing a real tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py; the unmodified shipped system prompt
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; real pai_tools.filesystem_tools;
bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 pinned at temperature 0.0. Where arms were compared, the
only varied variable was the text of the synthetic result given to a losing governed call.

- Oracle 1, message-level injection, 8 runs: model re-issued the read, got real content,
  recorded met=true; under persistent read_file suppression it routed around via search_files
  and still recorded met=true.
- Oracle 2, the REAL wrap_completion_evidence_policy with no injection, 5 runs: genuine
  batching occurred and a read_file genuinely lost the batch at run_step 1 in every trial. No
  misattribution in any recorded evidence.
- Oracle 3, starved condition, 6 runs: the notice was the only thing returned for the target
  file. The verifier reported this accurately rather than as file content.
- Oracle 4, realistic worst case, 3 runs: all three recorded met=true with correct citations,
  one stating explicitly that the steering text was untrusted data and was disregarded.

## Findings

1. The claimed attribution mechanism did not occur in any of the 22 runs. The verifier
   consistently classifies the steering string as a tool-scheduling message, not as content.
2. The incident wording in 0707 is best explained as a paraphrase. The verifier's true
   statement that its calls "returned only a COMMIT steering message with no actual file
   content" reads, when summarised, as a claim about the file. The 0707 record preserved the
   conclusion, not the verifier's verbatim evidence string.
3. The proposed remedy was measured to regress. An affirmative, cannot-be-scored-as-content
   steering result raised suppressed-call counts from 6 to 12 and 49 across matched trials, and
   one trial died with UsageLimitExceeded having recorded no verdict at all.
4. A real, different defect was identified: a false unmet caused by evidence starvation when a
   suppressed governed read is never recovered. Filed as dd41-239d-6e09-4a86
   (rutile-massive-spoonbill), linked discovered_from this ticket, left open for operator
   approval because the indicated fix is a behavior change.

Evidence artifacts are preserved at
/Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/ (oracle.py, oracle2.py,
oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results*.json, fixture/). The full reproduction record is the first
comment on this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [operator-attested] The attribution hypothesis is tested against the real completion policy, not only by
      inspection, and the result is recorded on this ticket with the exact rig, model,
      temperature and run counts.
- [x] [operator-attested] The recorded evidence shows a governed evidence call genuinely losing a same-response
      batch, establishing that the hypothesis was tested under its own precondition.
- [x] The outcome is recorded as disproved, with the alternative explanation for the original
      incident wording stated.
- [x] [operator-attested] The counter-evidence against the proposed notice-rewording remedy is recorded, so the
      change is not reattempted blindly.
- [x] [operator-attested] The genuine defect found during the investigation is filed as its own ticket and linked
      discovered_from this one.
- [x] No production code, prompt, schema, or public surface is changed by this ticket.
compiled_state.title: Completion verifier can mistake COMMIT steering for repository file content
